latest_release.name: rig-v0.46.0
latest_release.body:
### Added

- *(rig-mcp-client)* new plugin crate `rig-mcp-client` (`rig_mcp_client::McpPlugin`), listed off in the default `plugins.toml`: MCP servers' tools (stdio and streamable HTTP) as `<server>__<tool>`, from `$RIG_HOME/mcp.json` and `<project>/.rig/mcp.json`. A project's server starts only once approved as written (`/mcp approve`, `/mcp deny`); `/mcp add` and `/mcp remove` edit the right file. `McpCorePlugin` and `AddMcpServer` let a front add its client's servers for one run. The `mcpServers` format with `type`, `disabled` and `${VAR}` expansion, with other fields refused by name for that server only, and `[mcp] connect_timeout_secs` (30). A sessionless run starts no `mcp.json` server. Headless `--tools` can name a tool a plugin registers in the background, such as `<server>__<tool>` (by [gold-silver-copper](https://github.com/gold-silver-copper)) ([#2938](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/pull/2938), [#2948](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/pull/2948))
- *(rig-acp)* `rig acp`, an optional plugin: the coding agent for ACP v1 clients (Zed, Neovim plugins), with a rig process per session, rig's models, sign-in, tools, sessions and slash commands, permissions and forms, client MCP servers through rig-mcp-client, and history replayed from rig's own session (by [gold-silver-copper](https://github.com/gold-silver-copper)) ([#2948](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/pull/2948))
- *(rig-claude-cloak)* an opt-in Linux and macOS plugin for Anthropic subscription OAuth and compatible request shaping under a separate `claude-cloak/*` provider, published with every release as `rig-claude-cloak` and listed disabled in the default `plugins.toml` (by [gold-silver-copper](https://github.com/gold-silver-copper)) ([#2875](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/pull/2875), [#2891](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/pull/2891))
- *(rig-traffic)* new default plugin `rig_traffic::TrafficPlugin`: `--traffic-log`, or `[traffic] log = true` in `settings.toml`, records every model provider exchange in the session's `traffic.jsonl`, beside `effects.jsonl`. It runs on `rig-cassette`'s `traffic::TrafficLog` (feature `traffic`), which writes each exchange as one scrubbed, versioned JSON line (by [gold-silver-copper](https://github.com/gold-silver-copper)) ([#2893](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/pull/2893))
- *(rig-basics)* `AgentsMdPlugin` puts the `AGENTS.md` files from the working directory up to the repository root, and `RIG_HOME/AGENTS.md`, in the system prompt. `SkillsPlugin` lists skills (`SKILL.md`, the Agent Skills format) from `.rig/skills`, `.agents/skills`, `RIG_HOME/skills` and `~/.agents/skills`, with `/skill:<name> [text]`. `/login <provider>` saves a provider's API key, used before its environment variable, and `/logout` removes it (by [gold-silver-copper](https://github.com/gold-silver-copper)) ([#2873](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/pull/2873))
- *(sqlite, postgres)* `SqliteSessionStore` and `PostgresSessionStore` (feature `memory`): rig-memory sessions kept in a database shared by every process or worker. The facade's `memory` feature enables them with `sqlite` or `postgres`; `rig_memory::conformance::check_store` (feature `test-utils`) is the contract suite a store runs (by [gold-silver-copper](https://github.com/gold-silver-copper)) ([#2890](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/pull/2890))
- *(memory)* `rig_memory::migration`: a chain of whole-session format steps the agent runs when it opens a session in an earlier format, keeping a copy of the session as it was. The shipped chain has no step. `rig_memory::summarized_in_log` reports what each compaction took out (by [gold-silver-copper](https://github.com/gold-silver-copper)) ([#2899](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/pull/2899), [#2918](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/pull/2918))
- *(agent)* `AgentBuilder::provider_tool` and `provider_tools`: provider-hosted tools ride on every request the agent makes, after its function tools, and satisfy `ToolChoic

detail.readme:
[📑 Docs](https://rig.rs/docs)   •   [🌐 Website](https://rig.rs)   •   [🤝 Contribute](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/issues/new)   •   [✍🏽 Blogs](https://rig.rs/docs/guides)   •  
Rig is a Rust library for building LLM applications, and `rig`, a terminal coding agent built on it that you extend with Bevy plugins. ## The coding agent `rig-cli` is not on crates.io yet. Until the next release, install the last release, 0.46.0, whose `rig` crate carries the launcher: ```bash cargo install rig ``` This README describes `main`. 0.46.0 keeps its plugin list in `plugins.toml`, and [its guide](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/blob/v0.46.0/docs/agent.md) is on its tag. Or install `main` from a checkout (`--force` replaces a `rig` installed by another crate): ```bash git clone https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig && cd rig cargo install --locked --force --path crates/rig-cli ``` Then: 1. `rig` builds the agent, which takes several minutes the first time, and opens it. 2. `/login` signs in with a ChatGPT plan or saves a provider's API key. Or export a key, such as `OPENAI_API_KEY`, before starting `rig`. 3. `/model` picks a model. A local Ollama or llama.cpp server is listed once `OLLAMA_API_BASE_URL` or `LLAMACPP_API_BASE_URL` names it, or its key variable is set. 4. Type a prompt and press Enter. `/help` lists the commands. 5. `rig -p "fix the failing test"` answers one prompt without the terminal view. `rig update` updates rig ([how](docs/agent.md#update)). The agent guide also says what is [per home and what is per project](docs/agent.md#what-is-per-home-and-what-is-per-project). - **Everything is a plugin.** The agent is a [Bevy](https://bevy.org) app; its tools, commands, sessions, sign-in and terminal view are each a plugin, turned on or off in `settings.toml`, so any of them can be removed, replaced or added to. - **It rebuilds itself.** `/reload` rebuilds the agent with your plugin crates and restarts it in the same session, and keeps the old build running if the new one does not compile. `rig update` reinstalls rig with cargo; `/update` does it from the agent and restarts on it. Both arrive with the next release: 0.46.0 updates by installing again. - **Scriptable.** `rig -p --json` and `rig --json` drive it over pipes; `rig help-agents` is the protocol. - **More when you want it.** Subagents are an optional plugin, and the tools work on remote hosts over ssh or any command. The [agent guide](docs/agent.md) covers the keys, sessions, compaction, plugins and files, and the [plugin guide](crates/rig-harness/PLUGINS.md) shows how to write a tool, command or panel. The agent needs Rust 1.97.1 or newer and runs on Linux and macOS. ## The library ```bash cargo add rig ``` ```rust use rig::prelude::*; use rig::providers::openai::{self, OpenAI}; #[tokio::main] async fn main() -> Result<(), anyhow::Error> { // The client reads `OPENAI_API_KEY` and builds the models it serves. let model = OpenAI::from_env()?.completion(openai::GPT_6_1_SOL); let comedian = AgentBuilder::new(model) .preamble("You are a comedian here to entertain the user using humour and jokes.") .build(); let response = comedian.prompt("Entertain me!").await?; println!("{}", response.output()); Ok(()) } ``` The example also needs tokio, with the `macros` and `rt-multi-thread` features that `#[tokio::main]` uses, and anyhow (`cargo add tokio --features macros,rt-multi-thread` and `cargo add anyhow`). - 20+ model providers and 10+ vector stores, each under one interface - Agents with tools, multi-turn streaming and typed hooks - Completion, embedding, transcription, audio and image generation - [GenAI semantic conventions](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/) for OpenTelemetry - Recording and replay of an agent's effects ([`rig-cassette`](crates/rig-cassette/README.md)) - Browser WASM (`wasm32-unknown-unknown`) for the core and the agent runtime ([target support](crates/rig-agent/README.md#target-support)) More in [`examples/`](examples), the [docs](https://rig.rs/docs) and the [API reference](https://docs.rs/rig/latest/rig/). ## Crates The `rig` crate re-exports `rig-core`, and each companion crate behind a feature. | Crate | Feature | What it is | | --- | --- | --- | | [`rig-core`](crates/rig-core) | always | Provider-neutral messages, completion and embedding models, tool contracts, the conversation type, vector-store contracts, and the providers | | [`rig-agent`](crates/rig-agent) | `agent` (default) | The agent builder, prompting and streaming, hooks, the tool registry and the serializable `AgentRun` | | [`rig-memory`](crates/rig-memory) | `memory` | Windows, compaction, and saving, resuming and forking conversations | | [`rig-cassette`](crates/rig-cassette) | `cassette` | Effect logs: recording, replay and checkpoints | The coding agent's crates are not facade features. Depend on them directly. | Crate | What it is | | --- | --- | | [`rig-cli`](crates/rig-cli) | The `rig` launcher | | [`rig-tools`](crates/rig-tools) | Coding tools any rig agent can use: read, write, edit, search, shell | | [`rig-ecs`](crates/rig-ecs), [`rig-harness`](crates/rig-harness) | The agent kernel on Bevy's ECS, and the harness the coding agent's plugins build on | | [`rig-tui`](plugins/rig-tui), [`rig-basics`](plugins/rig-basics) | The terminal view, and the coding agent's default plugins | | [`rig-markdown`](crates/rig-markdown) | Markdown drawn as styled lines and word-wrapped to a width, shared by the terminal view and `rig -p` | | [`rig-fold`](plugins/rig-fold) | Off by default: folds finished tool calls in the terminal view, with a key that shows them whole | | [`rig-traffic`](plugins/rig-traffic) | Opt-in provider HTTP recording in the session store, using the cassette engine | | [`rig-mcp-client`](plugins/rig-mcp-client) | The coding agent's MCP client, off by default: MCP servers' tools, with an opt-in plugin that asks before a project's server starts | | [`rig-acp`](plugins/rig-acp) | `rig acp`, off by default: the coding agent for ACP clients (editors such as Zed) | ### Integrations ```toml rig = { version = "0.46.0", features = ["lancedb", "fastembed"] } ``` | Integration | Crate | Feature | Module path | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | AWS Bedrock | [`rig-bedrock`](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/tree/main/crates/rig-bedrock) | `bedrock` | `rig::bedrock` | | AWS S3Vectors | [`rig-s3vectors`](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/tree/main/crates/rig-s3vectors) | `s3vectors` | `rig::s3vectors` | | Candle (local Llama/SmolLM2/Qwen3 tools, YOLOv8 pose) | [`rig-candle`](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/tree/main/crates/rig-candle) | `candle` | `rig::candle` | | Cloudflare Vectorize | [`rig-vectorize`](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/tree/main/crates/rig-vectorize) | `vectorize` | `rig::vectorize` | | FastEmbed | [`rig-fastembed`](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/tree/main/crates/rig-fastembed) | `fastembed` | `rig::fastembed` | | Google Gemini gRPC | [`rig-gemini-grpc`](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/tree/main/crates/rig-gemini-grpc) | `gemini-grpc` | `rig::gemini_grpc` | | Google Vertex AI | [`rig-vertexai`](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/tree/main/crates/rig-vertexai) | `vertexai` | `rig::vertexai` | | HelixDB | [`rig-helixdb`](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/tree/main/crates/rig-helixdb) | `helixdb` | `rig::helixdb` | | LanceDB | [`rig-lancedb`](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/tree/main/crates/rig-lancedb) | `lancedb` | `rig::lancedb` | | Conversations over time | [`rig-memory`](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/tree/main/crates/rig-memory) | `memory` | `rig::memory` | | Milvus | [`rig-milvus`](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/tree/main/crates/rig-milvus) | `milvus` | `rig::milvus` | | MongoDB | [`rig-mongodb`](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/tree/main/crates/rig-mongodb) | `mongodb` | `rig::mongodb` | | Neo4j | [`rig-neo4j`](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/tree/main/crates/rig-neo4j) | `neo4j` | `rig::neo4j` | | PostgreSQL (vector store; with `memory`, a session store) | [`rig-postgres`](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/tree/main/crates/rig-postgres) | `postgres` | `rig::postgres` | | Qdrant | [`rig-qdrant`](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/tree/main/crates/rig-qdrant) | `qdrant` | `rig::qdrant` | | ScyllaDB | [`rig-scylladb`](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/tree/main/crates/rig-scylladb) | `scylladb` | `rig::scylladb` | | SQLite (vector store; with `memory`, a session store) | [`rig-sqlite`](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/tree/main/crates/rig-sqlite) | `sqlite` | `rig::sqlite` | | SurrealDB | [`rig-surrealdb`](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/rig/tree/main/crates/rig-surrealdb) | `surrealdb` | `rig::surrealdb` | | TypeSafe Jev (experimental judgments) | [`rig-typesafeai`](crates/rig-typesafeai) | `typesafeai` | `rig::typesafeai` | ## Community Projects built on Rig are listed in [awesome-rig](https://github.com/0xPlaygrounds/awesome-rig); open a pull request there to add yours. Questions and ideas are welcome on [Discord](https://discord.gg/playgrounds), and [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) says how to contribute. Rig is MIT licensed. > [!WARNING] > Rig is pre-1.0. Releases contain breaking changes; each release's > [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) and [migration notes](MIGRATING.md) say what > changed and how to move.
